overall: A curious, warm, lightly amused neighbor telling you about the strangest way dinner ever showed up, never selling it. The arc opens playful and lifted on the dog, settles into plain explanation through the middle, drops to its quietest and most certain on the companies' own words and the target that is not a count, then closes warm and a little wry.

lines.text: A dog guards this gate for the delivery driver. Dinner is coming. It refuses to land.
lines.intent: Cold open, a small joke set up and landed
lines.note: Emphasis on guards, then on refuses. Dry smile in the voice, no wink.

lines.text: In Spring, north of Houston, people became the first in the country to order Uber Eats by Zipline drone, on Tuesday, November 17th. Open the app, and pick by drone on the home screen.
lines.intent: Plant the where and when, then the simple action
lines.note: Spring is the town, say it plainly. Weight on first. The date is delivered as a fact, flat. Second sentence is easy and matter of fact, like showing a friend the phone.

lines.text: Then the drone picks up the order, and flies it to the customer.
lines.intent: Hand off, the machine takes over
lines.note: Weight on by itself. Light curiosity, unhurried.

lines.text: As it takes off, its weather sensors measure the wind.
lines.intent: A small detail that shows care
lines.note: Weight on measure. Quiet, observational, almost an aside.

lines.text: It cruises at about 300 feet, at up to 70 miles an hour. It can carry eight pounds as far as 10 miles.
lines.note: Each figure lands flat with no lift on the unit. Weight on eight pounds.

lines.text: Rain doesn't ground it. Small microphones listen for nearby aircraft, as far as 1.25 miles away, the company says.
lines.intent: Two small marvels, with the source kept honest
lines.note: Slight delight on listen. The attribution, the company says, is dropped lower and drier, a quiet honesty.

lines.text: Over the yard, it never lands. It hovers, and the pod comes down on a tether.
lines.intent: The central image, the payoff of the hook
lines.note: Weight on never, then a warm descending read on tether, as if watching it come down.

lines.text: Zipline says it stays roughly 330 feet up to deliver. Other delivery drones average 32 feet. Its chief executive, Keller Cliffton, says staying that high keeps it very quiet.
lines.intent: Comparison with the claim kept attributed
lines.note: Weight on 330 and then on 32, the contrast does the work. Keller Cliffton said clearly and evenly. Very quiet is read almost quietly.

lines.text: Zipline calls the system fully robotic and autonomous. An Uber executive says it reaches homes in under 10 minutes. Those are the companies' own words.
lines.intent: Mark the claims as claims, the honest turn
lines.note: Dry and even. Weight on says and on own. The last sentence is the quietest in the first half, level and certain, no lift.

lines.text: A person still watches. Zipline's remote pilots can override a flight path if there is a safety issue.
lines.intent: Human in the loop, a reassuring fact
lines.note: Weight on person. Warm and steady, close to the listener.

lines.text: Drone delivery is new to Spring. It is not new to Zipline. In Round Rock, a high school drone team placed and received the first order.
lines.intent: Widen the view, a little history with a smile
lines.note: Weight on new, then on not new, a gentle turn. Round Rock said the Texas way. The last sentence carries a small amused warmth on high school.

lines.text: Zipline says it has already made 1 million drone deliveries around Dallas alone.
lines.intent: A big number given as the company's claim
lines.note: Weight on 1 million, delivered flat and not sold. Zipline says stays attributed and unhurried.

lines.text: The goal is 1 million deliveries a day with Uber by 2029. That is a target, not a count.
lines.intent: The most important caution, said plainly
lines.note: The quietest, most certain line of the film. Number flat, no lift. Weight on target, then on count, level and dry.

lines.text: Back in Spring, a hand takes the sack, and nobody has to tip. The dog still barks, just at the sky now.
lines.intent: Button, warm landing on the joke
lines.note: Settle lower than the middle and more certain, a smile at the end. Weight on sky, and let the last words fall softly, no rise.
